statements.text: ILO 12: Develop and execute experiments to validate design assumptions, analyze system behaviors, and refine solutions, demonstrating an understanding of experimental design and data collection principles. [CLO 3] [CLO4]

Case Study Discussion: Systems Engineering as a Human Activity Provide a case study that highlights the role of human factors in systems engineering, including team dynamics, stakeholder involvement, and ethical considerations. Facilitate a class discussion on the human-centered aspects and their impact on project outcomes. Design and Conduct Experiments Activity Assign students a mini- project to design and conduct an experiment to validate a system component or process. They should identify the objective, develop a methodology, collect data, and analyze results to inform design improvements. Robust Design Brainstorming Session (Robust Design I) In small groups, students brainstorm how to apply basic robust design principles to make a system more stable under varying conditions. They discuss factors that influence system stability and propose design adjustments to minimize variability. Advanced Robust Design Project (Robust Design II) Activity: For a more complex project, students apply advanced robust design techniques to a hypothetical or real-world system. They identify and control multiple variables to minimize performance variation across diverse scenarios.

weekContext.content: Application • Systems Engineering As Human Activity • Trade Space Exploration Concept Selection • Experiments • Robust Design I • Robust Design II

Design and Conduct Experiments Activity Assign students a mini- project to design and conduct an experiment to validate a system component or process. They should identify the objective, develop a methodology, collect data, and analyze results to inform design improvements. Robust Design Brainstorming Session (Robust Design I) In small groups, students brainstorm how to apply basic robust design principles to make a system more stable under varying conditions. They discuss factors that influence system stability and propose design adjustments to minimize variability. Advanced Robust Design Project (Robust Design II) Activity: For a more complex project, students apply advanced robust design techniques to a hypothetical or real-world system. They identify and control multiple variables to minimize performance variation across diverse scenarios.
weekContext.assessment: Robust Design I – System Evaluation and Improvement Proposal Task: Have students apply basic robust design techniques to evaluate a system and propose design changes that would make it more stable under varying conditions. They should identify critical factors that affect performance and suggest improvements to minimize variability. Robust Design II – Advanced Design Analysis Task: For a more complex system, students should apply advanced robust design methods to assess and improve the system’s performance. They will use tools such as design of experiments (DOE) to explore multiple design variables and their interactions. Robust Design Report (I & II) Task: Students will submit a report for each part of the robust design application, detailing the steps taken to assess and improve system performance. For Robust Design I, they will focus on basic principles, and for Robust Design II, they will apply advanced techniques to optimize the system.
